en: My child, if you want freedom, give up the pleasures of the senses as if they were poison, and drink in forgiveness, honesty, kindness, purity and truth as if they were nectar.
Low people who reveal each other's secret weak points destroy themselves, like a snake trapped inside an anthill.
The Creator gave no scent to gold, no fruit to sugarcane, no flowers to sandalwood; he did not make the learned rich or kings long-lived. It seems no one was there to advise him.
Nectar is the chief of all medicines, food is the chief of all comforts, the eye is the chief of all senses, and the head is the chief of all parts of the body.

first: दुतो न सञ्चरति खे न चलेच्च वार्ता ।
en: No messenger travels through the sky, no news comes from there, no one said it before, and no one has gone there; yet the Brahmin who can tell when the sun and moon will be eclipsed, how is he not learned?
Wake these seven if they are sleeping: a student, a servant, a traveller, a hungry person, a frightened person, a storekeeper and a gatekeeper.

first: अहिं नृपं च शार्दुलं बरटि बालकं तथा ।
en: Do not wake these seven if they are sleeping: a snake, a king, a tiger, a wasp, a small child, someone else's dog and a fool.
Brahmins who study the Vedas for money and live on the food of low people, what can they do? They are like snakes without poison.

first: यस्मिन रुष्टे भयं नास्ति तुष्टे नैव धनागमः ।
en: If a person's anger causes no fear and his pleasure brings no reward, if he can neither punish nor help, what can his anger do?
Even a snake with no poison should raise a big hood; whether there is poison or not, the show alone frightens.
The wise pass their time in the morning with a story about gambling, at midday with a story about a woman, and at night with a story about a thief.
A garland strung with one's own hands, sandal paste ground with one's own hands, and a text written with one's own hands would take away the glory even of Indra.
Sugarcane, sesame, a lowly person, a woman, gold, earth, sandalwood, curd and betel leaf: these improve when they are pressed or rubbed.
Poverty is made bright by courage, old clothes by keeping them clean, poor food by serving it hot, and plain looks by good character.
